message.reasoning:
We need to produce a test class code that covers the test cases described. Already there is a test class with a single test method that verifies delegation. We need to expand to cover more cases: delegation tests for various indices, including negative, out of bounds, ensure exception propagation, verify exact call count, edge index tests for 0 and last valid index, and seriesBarCount (one past last) causing exception.

We need to mock MMAIndicator behavior to throw IndexOutOfBoundsException for certain indices. Since MMAIndicator is constructed via mockConstruction, we can set up behavior per index using thenAnswer or thenReturn with condition.

We also need to set up series bar count. ATRIndicator likely uses getBarCount() from averageTrueRangeIndicator; but we can mock averageTrueRangeIndicator's getBarCount? Actually MMAIndicator has method getBarCount() returning series.getBarCount(). We can mock MMAIndicator's getBarCount to return a specific value.

But ATRIndicator constructor signature? Not shown fully, but we see new ATRIndicator(mockTR, 5). So ATRIndicator takes TRIndicator and time frame (period). It internally creates MMAIndicator with the TRIndicator and period. So we mock its construction to return a mock MMAIndicator.

Thus we can set up the mock's getValue behavior: for index 5, return expectedNum; for index 0, return expectedNum0; for lastValidIndex (e.g., barCount-1), return expectedNumLast; for negative or out of range, throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

We need to know barCount. We can set barCount = 10 for example. So lastValidIndex = 9. seriesBarCount = 10.

We need to configure the mock construction to set behavior based on index. Use when(mock.getValue(anyInt())).thenAnswer(invocation -> { int idx = invocation.getArgument(0); if (idx <0 || idx >= barCount) throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(...); else return ... }).

But we also need to verify call count for specific test.

We also need parameterized tests for delegation cases.

We'll keep existing @BeforeEach that sets up expectedNum for default index 5. We'll modify to set up barCount variable and configure behavior accordingly.

We'll add tests:

- parameterized test for valid indices (5,0,9) expecting returned Num matches appropriate mock.

- test for negative index expecting IndexOutOfBoundsException.

- test for out-of-range index (1000, seriesBarCount) expecting exception.

- test verifying getValue called exactly once for index 3.

We can use @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource.

Need to import necessary JUnit5 parameterized.

We'll also need to capture the mocked MMAIndicator instance.

Implementation details:

In @BeforeEach, after mocking construction, we can store reference to the mock: MMAIndicator mockedMMA = mmaConstruction.constructed().get(0); then configure its behavior.

But the mockConstruction lambda provides each mock instance; we can configure inside there using context. We'll set up a shared barCount variable defined as a field, set in @BeforeEach.

Simplify: In @BeforeEach, after mmaConstruction = mockConstruction(...), we can get the mock from mmaConstruction.constructed().get(0) and set up behavior using when(mock.getValue(anyInt()))... but we need per-index behavior.

We'll create a map of index to Num.

Define Num num5 = mock(Num.class); etc.

We'll set up when(mock.getValue(eq(5))).thenReturn(num5); etc.

And for any other index, we can default to throwing.

Use when(mock.getValue(argThat(i -> i <0 || i >= barCount))).thenThrow(new IndexOutOfBoundsException());

But Mockito doesn't allow overlapping stubs? We'll use thenAnswer.

Implement:

when(mock.getValue(anyInt())).thenAnswer(invocation -> {
    int idx = invocation.getArgument(0);
    if (idx == 5) return num5;
    if (idx == 0) return num0;
    if (idx == barCount-1) return numLast;
    throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException("Invalid index: " + idx);
});

Also set up mock.getBarCount() to return barCount.

Now tests can use atrIndicator.getValue(index) and assert appropriate.

For exception tests, use assertThrows.

For verify call count test (index 3), we need to set up behavior for index 3 to return some Num (maybe num3). Then after calling, verify(mockedMMA, times(1)).getValue(3); Also verify no more interactions.

Edge: In that test, we need to ensure MMAIndicator returns a Num for index 3 to avoid exception. So we need to stub for idx 3 as well.

Thus in setup we can stub for all indices 0..barCount-1 to return a generic mock Num perhaps same instance or index-specific.

Simplify: create a generic Num genericNum = mock(Num.class); and for any valid index return genericNum.

But earlier we want distinct for test verification of return value; we can just assertSame(genericNum). That's fine.

Thus we can set up:

when(mock.getValue(anyInt())).thenAnswer(invocation -> {
    int idx = invocation.getArgument(0);
    if (idx <0 || idx >= barCount) throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException();
    return genericNum;
});

Then tests for valid indices will just assertSame(genericNum). That's okay.

But we also have earlier expectedNum used in existing test for index 7. Could adjust to generic.

Simplify: keep expectedNum as generic for all valid indices.

Thus modify @BeforeEach to set up generic behavior.

Now write tests.

Add imports: org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest; org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.CsvSource; org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.ValueSource; etc.

Implement test methods:

- @ParameterizedTest(name = "valid index {0}") with @ValueSource(ints = {0,5,9}) expecting same generic Num.

- @ParameterizedTest(name = "invalid index {0}") with @ValueSource(ints = {-1,10,1000}) expecting IndexOutOfBoundsException.

- @Test void testGetValueCallsExactlyOnce() for index 3, verify call count.

Make sure to get mockedMMA via mmaConstruction.constructed().get(0) inside each test (or store as field).

Add comments.

Now produce final code.
